Constraint Handling Rules (CHR) is a declarative, constraint-based programming language that has been proven Turing complete when utilizing a constraint system capable of exponential-time computation. However, a specific subset of CHR known as "single head rules," where each rule contains only one head, was previously suspected to lack Turing completeness. This paper demonstrates that even with single head rules, CHR remains Turing complete provided the underlying constraint theory supports at least polynomial-time computation. We establish this by constructing an abstract Turing machine capable of simulating any CHR program. This simulation relies on a specific encoding method that translates the CHR state into the configuration of the Turing machine. Furthermore, we prove that this encoding is efficient, requiring only polynomial time and space to encode and decode.

We introduce a new method for analyzing galaxy spin directions, which are typically represented as unit vectors on a sphere. This approach utilizes the spherical Fourier transform to decompose the distribution into spherical harmonics, offering a straightforward and computationally efficient means to characterize the large-scale arrangement of spin orientations. This technique is applied to a sample of 100,000 galaxies from the SDSS-III BOSS survey, covering a sky area of 10,000 square degrees. The resulting analysis reveals that the spin directions are broadly isotropic, with no statistically significant evidence of preferred orientations. Furthermore, we examine the galaxy spin directions in relation to the large-scale matter distribution, quantified by the matter power spectrum, finding no significant correlation between the two.

Meta-learning has emerged as a robust approach to few-shot learning, yet meta-learners face significant challenges when dealing with limited data, as they often struggle to identify useful patterns and risk overfitting to noise. To address these issues, we introduce a new meta-learning framework that integrates a self-supervised learning component to leverage unlabeled data. This approach utilizes a task-specific self-supervised module to generate pseudo-labels, which are then used to train a meta-model capable of classifying new tasks with only a few labeled examples. Our method is evaluated across several few-shot classification benchmarks, demonstrating that it outperforms existing meta-baseline approaches.

The growing application of deep learning in neuroimaging has significantly advanced the identification of neurological phenotypes, yet these models often function as opaque "black boxes," hindering the interpretation of their findings. To address this limitation, we introduce a new framework that leverages generative deep learning to create interpretable representations of neurological phenotypes. Our approach utilizes a variational autoencoder to learn a latent space of phenotypes, enabling the generation of brain images corresponding to specific trait values. We validated this method using a dataset of 1,000 individuals from the UK Biobank, focusing on a neurological trait: the presence of a neurological disorder. Our results demonstrate that the generated brain images exhibit realistic anatomical features and accurately reflect the neurological trait of interest. Furthermore, we show that the model can successfully localize the neuroanatomical correlates of the trait, indicating that the learned representations are both realistic and biologically meaningful.

This study introduces a taxonomy of AI Ethics literature, constructed by analyzing 1,000+ articles from the FAccT conference spanning 2009 to 2019. We categorize these works into three domains: Theory, Practice, and Education, further dividing them into subcategories. We demonstrate that these works are unevenly distributed across time and subject areas, with a notable rise in the number of publications since 2015. Additionally, we identify the primary subjects within each category and examine the relationships between them. We also assess the citation patterns of works across different categories and subcategories. Ultimately, this research offers a comprehensive overview of the field's current state and provides a structured framework for future work.

We demonstrate that enriching a non-trivial finite alphabet with a new neutral symbol and extending the logical framework of second-order monodic logic (MSO) applied to words of length $\omega$ results in a system capable of defining all first-order sentences. This enhancement effectively elevates the expressive capacity of these logics beyond their traditional limitations.

In large-scale dynamic wireless networks, the sheer volume of nodes and the constant shifts in their positions and channel conditions create substantial overhead for channel estimation. This paper introduces a new method to mitigate such overhead by leveraging the inherent sparsity of channels. The proposed approach utilizes a two-stage architecture: initially, a dedicated estimation module recovers the sparse channel vector for every node, followed by a compression module that reduces the data required for transmission. This compression is achieved by mapping the channel vector into a lower-dimensional space via matrix multiplication, thereby shrinking the overhead. Crucially, the design incorporates a specific constraint on the compression matrix to ensure that the sparse nature of the channels remains intact after reduction. Theoretically, the study establishes the necessary conditions for the existence of such a compression matrix and analyzes the resulting estimation error. Furthermore, the paper presents a practical construction algorithm for the compression matrix and validates the approach through simulations, demonstrating that the method significantly lowers channel estimation overhead in large-scale networks.

We present a new determination of the $V_{ud}$ matrix element, which characterizes beta decay, utilizing the most recent precise experimental data. This analysis relies on a comprehensive theoretical framework encompassing radiative corrections, recoil effects, and nuclear structure considerations. By employing a consistent nuclear model, we achieve a $1.3\%$ precision, yielding the value $V_{ud} = 0.9243(20)$. This result aligns well with the Standard Model's prediction of $1.0000 \pm 0.0005$.

This paper introduces a new neural network architecture for image denoising, built upon a U-Net design enhanced with identity mappings. These mappings connect corresponding layers in the encoder and decoder, creating shortcuts that allow the model to retain critical details and textures. Additionally, the network incorporates a new loss function that integrates a standard mean squared error term with a term derived from the structural similarity index. Experimental results indicate that this approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art denoising techniques.

Multiview data representation is a critical challenge in machine learning, with a primary goal of creating a unified embedding that captures commonalities across different views while isolating view-specific information. While numerous methods have been developed to address this, they often rely on a restrictive assumption that all shared latent factors are linearly dependent on the observed multiview data. This paper introduces a novel multiview representation technique that utilizes a neural network to model the relationship between multiview data and shared components, thereby eliminating the need for the linearity constraint. This approach offers greater flexibility in modeling shared components, which is particularly advantageous when dealing with nonlinear relationships. We validate the method's effectiveness through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art multiview representation methods.

We present a novel class of red outlier galaxies, defined as objects with red colors and low stellar masses that deviate from the main sequence. Utilizing a sample of 1,000,000 galaxies from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey Data Release 7, we identified these outliers by applying a color-based selection technique. Our analysis reveals that approximately 1,000,000 of these galaxies are powered by active galactic nuclei (AGNs), with a specific subset showing evidence of radio emission. These radio-luminous red outliers are typically low-mass systems containing young stellar populations and exhibit radio power levels comparable to those of radio-loud AGNs. Furthermore, a significant fraction of these galaxies display strong optical emission lines, indicating that they are optically selected AGNs. In contrast, a subset of red outliers lacks strong emission lines, suggesting that they are powered by star formation rather than AGNs. These findings demonstrate that radio-luminous red outliers are primarily optically selected AGNs, whereas non-emission-line outliers are driven by star formation.

A primary obstacle in AI research is ensuring that systems can effectively collaborate with humans on moral judgments. While recent studies have attempted to align AI with human values by utilizing human feedback, these methods often fail to account for the nuances of moral reasoning. Consequently, they struggle to distinguish between superficially similar yet fundamentally different moral judgments. To address this, we introduce a new approach that employs a generative adversarial network (GAN) to generate synthetic human judgments, thereby enabling the training of a more robust moral alignment model. Our method is designed to capture the underlying reasoning processes behind moral judgments, allowing the AI to differentiate between similar but distinct ethical decisions. Empirical results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in aligning AI with human values.

We demonstrate that any valuation ring which subsumes its residue field (and possesses a characteristic different from $p$) admits a primitive element. This result extends to a broader class of valuation rings, which are unramified and finitely ramified extensions of their base valuation rings, provided the base is Henselian.

We introduce a new approach for investigating quantum scarring within the framework of a two-dimensional Dirac equation. This technique is designed to be straightforward and broadly applicable, allowing for the identification of scarred eigenstates across a wide range of parameter values. Our findings demonstrate that the presence of scars in Dirac quantum systems is more prevalent than previously recognized.

Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (CACC) and platooning are emerging as promising solutions for enhancing traffic efficiency and safety. However, their widespread adoption is hindered by stringent requirements regarding communication reliability and vehicle automation. To address these challenges, this study introduces a new framework that leverages the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) to enable CACC and platooning. By utilizing the existing cellular infrastructure, this approach significantly reduces the dependency on dedicated communication networks. Consequently, it lowers the overall system costs while maintaining the necessary reliability for effective operation.

Social media platforms have become essential for individuals to share personal experiences and opinions on a wide range of topics. However, the sheer volume of user-generated content has created a significant challenge in distinguishing between authentic and fabricated posts. To address this, we introduce a method for assessing the credibility of social media users. Our approach utilizes a hybrid model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to analyze both the text and associated images of user profiles. This hybrid architecture is trained on a dataset comprising 10,000 user profiles, each labeled with a credibility score. The model's performance is evaluated using standard metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and the F1-score.

This study introduces a novel framework for delivering V2X services within 5G networks, utilizing network slicing to establish isolated, dedicated environments for each service. To address the challenge of allocating resources across these slices, we propose a new algorithm that determines the necessary resource blocks (RBs) for slice deployment. The approach is further enhanced by a new method for assigning these RBs to specific slices, which operates by identifying and utilizing network resources currently underutilized by other slices. Simulation results indicate that this proposed algorithm significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both efficiency and performance.

Human-robot collaboration (HRC) is a rapidly expanding field of research, with a growing emphasis on creating systems that enable seamless interaction between humans and robots. While recent studies have highlighted the potential of haptic feedback to enhance safety and efficiency within these collaborative environments, there remains a significant gap in understanding how different feedback modalities influence performance. This study addresses this gap by conducting a systematic review of current literature to evaluate the impact of haptic feedback on HRC. The analysis covers three primary dimensions: the specific haptic modalities employed, the types of tasks performed, and the resulting performance metrics. The findings indicate that haptic feedback is most frequently applied to force and vibration modalities, with the majority of research focusing on assembly tasks and performance evaluations based on speed and accuracy.

By 2050, the global urban population is expected to surge by 60%. This shift necessitates a fundamental reimagining of urban infrastructure, services, and planning to accommodate the influx of people and goods. Consequently, the Internet of Things (IoT) is poised to become a cornerstone of the urban environment, facilitating the deployment of smart devices and services. This paper examines the critical challenges facing urban IoT, specifically addressing the need for a new communication paradigm that supports diverse applications. We introduce the concept of "Urban Internet of Things" (UIoT) as a framework for analyzing these issues, while also exploring the transformative potential of 5G and beyond technologies. Finally, the study outlines a roadmap for the future of UIoT, highlighting key research directions and open questions.

This study examines the online caching problem with augmented predictions, where an online algorithm receives a forecast for the optimal offline cost. We introduce a novel prediction-augmented algorithm that achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ competitive ratio, provided the total $\ell_1$ prediction error is limited. Additionally, we present an algorithm with an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ competitive ratio under the constraint that the prediction is additive-optimal. We further investigate the scenario where the maximum possible prediction error is known, proposing a method with an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ competitive ratio for this setting. Finally, we evaluate the problem with a sliding window of length $w$, demonstrating that our proposed algorithm attains an $\mathcal{O}(1)$ competitive ratio when the prediction error relative to this window is bounded.

Precise segmentation of medical images is vital for diagnosis and treatment planning, yet it remains a challenging task due to the high variability in organ shapes and the presence of noise. This paper introduces a new framework called "Deep Learning with Attention and Multi-Scale Fusion" (Deep Learning with Attention and Multi-Scale Fusion) designed to address these issues. The proposed method employs a multi-scale fusion module to capture comprehensive contextual details and integrates an attention mechanism to highlight regions of interest, thereby enhancing segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both accuracy and computational efficiency.

We examine the eleven-dimensional supergravity background defined by a $G_2$-structure equipped with a closed, non-vanishing 3-form $\phi$. Our findings demonstrate that the equations of motion necessitate a specific relationship between the Hodge dual of $\phi$ and the $G_2$-structure spinor $\psi$. Leveraging this relationship, we establish that the geometry is either a product of a circle and a warped K3 surface or possesses a holonomy contained within the product of $SU(3)$ and $G_2$.

Machine learning models are frequently trained on datasets containing incorrect labels, which can degrade their performance and hinder generalization. This study introduces a novel approach to identifying and correcting mislabeled examples by leveraging the concept of label consistency. We demonstrate that a data point is likely wrongly labeled if its nearest neighbors possess different class labels. Our method utilizes a single reference model to detect these inconsistencies and correct labels by selecting the most appropriate alternative class. Experimental results indicate that this technique effectively identifies errors and improves the accuracy of various models across multiple datasets.

The Laughlin state at the $
u=1$ quantum Hall effect ground state is characterized by a Laughlin wave function, which is widely recognized as the Laughlin state. This paper introduces a new perspective on the $
u=1$ state, deriving it from a specific projection of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model onto the Laughlin state manifold. This approach offers a fresh insight into the $
u=1$ state, suggesting that the spin-1/2 Heisenberg model may serve as a more fundamental description of the quantum Hall effect than the Laughlin state itself.

This study introduces the novel METRO training strategy, which is designed to enhance the performance of language models during pretraining. By leveraging a specific loss function, METRO maximizes the mutual information between the model's latent representations and the original input data. We demonstrate that METRO effectively complements conventional language modeling techniques, yielding substantial improvements in downstream tasks. Our experiments reveal that the performance of models trained with METRO is highly sensitive to the choice of the parameter $\beta$. To address this, we develop a new adaptive method for determining optimal $\beta$ values, which significantly outperforms manual selection. Furthermore, we validate the efficacy of METRO across various domains, including English, Chinese, and Japanese, using both pretrained language models and the Transformer-XL architecture.

We examine how entropy-based metrics, including von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and entanglement entropy, characterize the topology of quantum networks. By applying these tools to a quantum version of the Ising model, we demonstrate that entropy enables the identification of phase transitions and the extraction of critical exponents. Furthermore, we analyze the dynamics of these entropic quantities during quantum state transfer across a network, revealing that they offer a superior method for characterizing the fidelity of such transfers compared to conventional approaches.

Data visualizations are essential for conveying insights, yet their impact relies heavily on the presenter's ability to guide the audience's attention and explain the visual's purpose. This study examines how specific presentation techniques—such as verbal introductions, signposting, and emphasis—affect viewers' comprehension and memory. We conducted a series of experiments involving 1,000 participants, who were randomly assigned to watch either silent or narrated video clips of data visualizations. Our findings indicate that clear verbal introductions and signposting significantly enhance understanding and recall, whereas cues regarding data source or specific emphasis had negligible effects. Additionally, we found that viewers of silent videos often misinterpreted the data, suggesting that these elements serve as critical scaffolding for comprehension.

We investigate the thermalization of a many-body quantum system under continuous driving, modeled as a spin chain subjected to a periodic Hamiltonian. We demonstrate that the resulting steady states are maximal entropy states, consistent with predictions from the generalized Gibbs ensemble. Our findings indicate that the system's temperature rises continuously with the amplitude of the drive. Furthermore, we observe that the system's entropy production rate is inversely proportional to the square of the drive's amplitude.

Counterfactual explanations are increasingly vital for interpreting machine learning predictions, and this paper introduces a novel approach to generating "counterfactual plans"—sequences of actions required to reach a desired outcome. We demonstrate that these plans are more informative than standard counterfactuals, which typically provide only a single attribute modification. Our method is evaluated across various domains, including tabular data, image classification, and natural language processing.

Urban sound classification is a vital component of monitoring noise levels in cities, yet it remains a challenging endeavor. This study introduces a novel approach to urban sound classification that leverages a graph-based representation of audio data. We utilize a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract features from audio segments, which are subsequently processed by a Graph Neural Network (GNN) to determine the class of each sound. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves state-of-the-art performance on the UrbanSound8K dataset.

This study examines $N=3$ gauged supergravity models in four anti-de Sitter dimensions ($AdS_4$) featuring symmetries of either $SO(3)\times SO(3)$ or $SO(3)$. We derive the corresponding black hole solutions for these theories, presenting their thermodynamic properties and analyzing the nature of their phase transitions.

Focal-plane Sensor-processors (FPSPs) are a promising technology for edge computing, offering high parallelism and low latency. These attributes are essential for handling the massive data streams generated by the proliferation of IoT devices. FPSPs are typically constructed using a combination of custom analog circuitry and ASICs, which are designed to execute specific algorithms. However, the specialized nature of these designs often restricts their flexibility. This paper introduces a novel FPSP architecture that integrates a programmable FPGA with a custom analog circuit to achieve both adaptability and high performance. The FPGA is interfaced with the sensor via a custom analog-to-digital converter (ADC) that converts analog signals into digital data. The FPGA is then programmed to run various algorithms, which are executed directly on the FPGA hardware. This approach allows for the rapid prototyping of new algorithms and facilitates their deployment on the FPGA hardware. The proposed architecture is evaluated using a range of algorithms, including object detection, image classification, and image segmentation. The results demonstrate that the proposed architecture achieves a significant improvement in both speed and energy efficiency compared to existing solutions.

We demonstrate that generalized $\theta$-terms, which are signatures of global symmetries, can emerge in effective field theories (EFTs) through the chiral anomaly of those symmetries. This relationship is expressed via a non-linear generalization of the Callan-Farber-Symanzik-Wess-Zumino (CFWSZ) anomaly equation. We further show that these generalized $\theta$-terms are essential for reconciling the chiral anomalies of EFTs with those of the underlying ultraviolet (UV) theory. Finally, we discuss the implications of our findings for the realization of global symmetries in quantum gravity.

This paper introduces a new oracle designed for empirical game-theoretic analysis, utilizing the concept of a core set to estimate the Nash equilibria of a game. This oracle is applied to the empirical analysis of the Rock-Scissors-Brick (RSB) game, which models the strategic interactions among three distinct groups of agents. We demonstrate that the oracle-driven approach successfully identifies equilibrium outcomes in the empirical RSB analysis, even when the dataset is limited in size.

This paper introduces a novel modal logic designed to formalize Aristotle's theory of modal syllogisms. The system employs a distinctive four-dimensional semantics, which facilitates the derivation of both modern and Aristotelian interpretations of modal propositions. We present a sound and complete axiomatization, demonstrate the derivation of a theorem-based system, and utilize a tableaux method to validate these results.

This paper introduces a new class of classical causal inequalities that are violated by quantum correlations. We demonstrate that these inequalities can serve as causal signatures for a specific set of nonlocal correlations that breach the causal limits established by Leggett and Dermer (Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 160405, 2006). To confirm these violations experimentally, we show that the required detection efficiency is less than 50%, which is attainable with current technology.

This study addresses frame-level bit allocation for HEVC/ H.265 intra-coded video sequences. We introduce a method that leverages the relationship between rate-distortion performance and the quantization parameter (QP) to determine optimal bit allocation. The approach first trains a neural network to estimate the QP for every frame, then assigns the quantization parameter for each block based on its estimated complexity. Experiments conducted on the JCT-BC and JCT-VC HE reference datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior coding efficiency compared to uniform quantization strategies.

The C/O ratio is a critical parameter for understanding the formation and evolution of planetary systems. In protoplanetary disks, this ratio is determined by the relative abundances of carbon and oxygen-bearing species, which vary with both radial distance and vertical height. While the vertical distribution of these species is well-documented, the radial abundance patterns remain largely unknown. This study investigates the radial abundance profiles of key carbon and oxygen carriers in the disk surrounding the young star TW Hya. We utilized the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to observe the $^{13}$C$^{34}$S, $^{13}$CS, and C$^{34}$S lines, alongside the $^{13}$CS and C$^{34}$S transitions. By analyzing the spatial distribution of these molecules, we determined the C/O ratio at various disk radii. Our findings indicate that the C/O ratio remains roughly constant at approximately 0.5 across the observed disk region, consistent with the solar value. This uniformity suggests that the C/O ratio in the disk is primarily governed by the underlying solar elemental composition.

Cutting planes are a fundamental component of solving mixed-integer linear programming (MILPs). This paper introduces a novel technique for deriving cutting planes by employing a neural network trained on the solution space of a specific MILP. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through experiments on quadratic knapsack problems, where the approach yields high-quality cuts that enhance solver performance.

We report on the synthesis of Ir$_{0.5}$Pt$_{0.5}$P$_2$, a material that exhibits topological semimetallic characteristics, as evidenced by the presence of Weyl points in the electronic band structure. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals a unique electronic band topology featuring intersecting electron and hole pockets. Furthermore, the observation of the chiral anomaly in the magnetotransport properties of this topological semimetal confirms its nature.

Duplicate detection within bug tracking systems offers significant advantages, such as streamlining maintenance workflows and enhancing the overall quality of the bug repository. However, existing research predominantly relies on supervised learning, which necessitates a substantial volume of manually labeled data. This study introduces a novel unsupervised approach to identify duplicate bug reports by leveraging the codebase alongside textual descriptions. The methodology involves extracting relevant code snippets from the bug report and the source code, followed by generating embeddings for each snippet using the Sentence-BERT model. These embeddings are then aggregated into a single vector representation for every report. The final classification of duplicates is determined by applying the K-Means clustering algorithm to these vectors. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed technique achieves an F1-score of 0.71, surpassing the performance of current state-of-the-art unsupervised methods.

We investigate the influence of anisotropy on the phase transition of the $O(3)$ non-linear $\sigma$-model within a two-dimensional lattice. By employing a renormalization group method, we derive scaling laws for the coupling constants and the critical exponents $\nu$ and $\eta$. Our findings indicate that anisotropy increases the critical coupling, thereby expanding the symmetric phase region. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the critical exponents remain independent of the anisotropy parameter, aligning with their continuum counterparts.

Distantly-Supervised Named Entity Recognition (DS-NER) is a zero-shot entity recognition method that leverages natural language sentences to automatically generate training data, effectively mitigating data scarcity. However, DS-NER often produces noisy labels due to the inherent ambiguity in sentence-based supervision. This study introduces a novel DS-NER framework that integrates a knowledge graph (KG) to enhance entity recognition. By employing a KG, the approach benefits from the robustness of structured knowledge, which helps alleviate noise and bias inherent in sentence-based supervision. Specifically, we propose a KG-augmented attention mechanism to extract entity-relevant features and a KG-based knowledge distillation strategy to refine the model's predictions. Experiments conducted on two datasets, DBpedia and CoNLL-2003, demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art models.

This study introduces a new dataset comprising 1,000 English tweets from the COVID-19 vaccination campaign on X (Twitter), annotated with sentiment labels and emotion categories. We evaluate various machine learning models for performing joint tasks of sentiment analysis and emotion detection. Our results indicate that a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network achieves the highest performance, surpassing other architectures like BERT and standard CNNs. Additionally, we examine how different hyperparameter configurations influence the accuracy of sentiment classification and emotion detection.

We examine the effective heat conductivity within highly heterogeneous, microstructured materials that exhibit a periodic structure at a scale much smaller than the sample's overall dimensions. Our analysis focuses on scenarios where the thermal conductivity tensor is not merely bounded but possesses a specific power-law decay in its off-diagonal elements. By applying a novel, quantitative framework for homogenization, we demonstrate that the effective conductivity tensor is well-defined and can be expressed through a weighted average of the periodic cell's properties. Furthermore, we establish precise estimates for the convergence rate of the homogenization process.

The planet CI Tau b, orbiting a young T Tauri star, is notable for its high eccentricity ($e = 0.51 \pm 0.05$) and long orbital period ($P = 11.1$ years). This study presents a comprehensive analysis of the system's orbital dynamics, utilizing a combination of radial velocity data from the Keck and Gemini observatories, alongside a new astrometric measurement from the VLT. The astrometric data, derived from a single epoch, is consistent with the radial velocity results and significantly refines the orbital period and semi-major axis constraints. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo approach to analyze the combined data, we determined that the planet's orbit is likely tilted relative to the star's disk. Furthermore, the orbit's high eccentricity suggests a history of significant dynamical evolution, potentially involving gravitational interactions with other bodies.

This study examines the force within a central force field by analyzing the particle's trajectory on an off-center circular path. The force's magnitude is determined by the radial distance from the center of force, expressed as $F(r) = F(r_0) (r/r_0)^n$, where $r$ represents the variable distance and $F(r_0)$ denotes the force's value at a fixed reference distance $r_0$. The research demonstrates that for any real value of the exponent $n$, an off-center circular solution to the equation of motion exists. Furthermore, it establishes that the velocity of such a particle is non-constant, with its direction changing at a non-uniform rate.

This paper introduces the definition of fractional Sobolev spaces for functions defined on the $k$-th order symmetric tensors over a compact Riemannian manifold $M$, alongside their corresponding fractional Poincaré inequalities. These results are derived through the utilization of Fourier series expansions for symmetric tensor fields and the analytical properties of Riesz potentials.

This paper introduces a new methodology for multi-object filtering that leverages multi-trajectory particle smoothers. The proposed approach estimates the posterior distribution of multi-object trajectories by utilizing a particle smoother that processes the output of any multi-object filter. This framework is inherently modular, accommodating a wide variety of multi-object filtering techniques. The authors present a straightforward and computationally efficient algorithm for estimating the posterior mean of the multi-object trajectory distribution. Additionally, the study proposes a new particle approximation for the multi-object posterior density, which is derived from a trajectory-wise particle smoother. This approximation is constructed by modifying the standard smoothing algorithm to incorporate an additional measurement noise model. The paper further outlines a method for computing the posterior mean of the multi-object density based on this approximation. Finally, the study evaluates the performance of the proposed approach through simulations using a synthetic scenario involving maneuvering targets.

The interaction between power electronics converters and weak AC networks presents significant stability challenges. This paper introduces a new framework for analyzing the stability of multi-converter systems, which incorporates the effects of converter control, grid impedance, and filter components. By employing a generalized mean value theorem, the system dynamics are simplified into a more manageable form, enabling the derivation of a stability condition applicable to multi-converter setups. Furthermore, a proposed method for assessing this condition is detailed, and a practical case study validates the proposed approach.

This study introduces a novel approach to online signature verification that leverages the specific characteristics of online signature dynamics. Our method characterizes templates using three metrics: the count of pen-up events, the count of pen-down events, and the sequence of these down-up actions. Our experiments indicate that integrating these features with existing online methods yields superior performance. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the three measures can be combined into a single, highly effective feature vector.

This note examines a problem of counting lattice points within a triangle, defined by its vertex coordinates. While the Gaussian point counting formula for polygons with integer coordinates is well-established, this work extends the principle to triangles where vertices are at points $(x_1, y_1)$, $(x_2, y_2)$, and $(x_3, y_3)$ belonging to a specific subring $R$ of $\mathbb{Q}$.

Context-aware programming (CoP) is a specialized approach designed to enhance mobile applications by utilizing a device's contextual data. This paper introduces a new context-oriented language, CoP, which integrates the core principles of context-awareness with the key features of context-field programming (CoP). The study details the syntax and operational mechanics of CoP, along with an examination of its implementation. The paper concludes by presenting the language's core capabilities through a case study that highlights its application in a real-world scenario.

This paper introduces a new attention-driven framework for pose estimation, designed to enhance the model's ability to focus on critical regions within images. Our approach utilizes a lightweight attention mechanism that integrates with the backbone network, enabling the model to capture both local and global visual features. This design facilitates the extraction of comprehensive information from images, thereby boosting the model's performance. Our method achieves state-of-the-art results on the PoseTrack 2021 dataset, with a significant improvement of 1.8% in the AOC metric compared to the previous leading method. Additionally, our approach offers notable computational advantages, delivering these results with only 1.5M parameters and 1.2G FLOPs.

We introduce a novel technique for measuring astrophysical fluxes by analyzing variations in detected counts from the Earth's occultation, a method particularly effective for high-energy gamma rays. This approach is applied to the blazar 3C 279, utilizing data from the Fermi-LAT Large Area Telescope. Our analysis of the source's light curve reveals a distinct dip corresponding to the Earth's shadow, which we attribute to the source's high inclination angle relative to our line of sight. By comparing the observed count rates before and during this occultation, we derive the source's flux. This method offers a unique advantage for Fermi-LAT, which typically struggles with flux normalization due to uncertainties in its effective area, and is applicable to any telescope capable of monitoring a source's light curve.

Blockchain protocols are designed to ensure fairness and security, yet their practical performance is heavily influenced by the specific implementation choices made. This paper introduces a framework for the formal analysis of blockchain protocol implementations, enabling the detection of implementation-level defects that compromise performance. We present a formal model of the Tendermint implementation of PBFT, along with a corresponding framework for analyzing implementation-specific properties. This approach facilitates the detection of implementation flaws, including deadlocks, through formal verification. We demonstrate the utility of this framework by identifying a deadlock occurring in Tendermint's commit phase, a failure that manifests when PBFT is executed on a single node.

This study examines the spectroscopy of doubly heavy tetraquark systems, denoted as $QQ\bar{q}\bar{q}$, where the quarks $QQ$ consist of two heavy flavors and the light quarks $\bar{q}\bar{q}$ consist of two light flavors. We employ the non-relativistic quark model, utilizing a non-relativistic potential to calculate the masses of these states. The results indicate that the lowest-lying tetraquark configurations, specifically $QQ[22^+]$ and $QQ[11^-]$, represent the most promising candidates for experimentally observed exotic particles.

We examine the implications of metastability for the electroweak vacuum within a framework where the Higgs mass is treated as a running parameter. Our analysis demonstrates that the vacuum remains stable at large scales provided the running Higgs mass does not exceed approximately 125 GeV. This finding is particularly relevant for extensions of the Standard Model, such as the Standard Model with a scalar singlet, where a heavier Higgs mass drives the vacuum toward instability at high scales.

We establish a novel upper bound for the global cost associated with the $p$-Logarithmic Sobolev inequality, which remains valid for any $p$-positive integer. The density power divergence (DPD) family, a recent development in robust statistics, is fundamentally linked to Bregman divergences. This study examines the asymptotic behavior of Bregman divergences derived from DPD estimators within a contaminated mixture framework. We demonstrate that, under suitable regularity conditions, the scaled estimator's distribution converges to a normal distribution, with explicitly calculated expressions for the asymptotic mean and variance. Furthermore, a novel U-statistic is proposed to estimate this asymptotic variance. The article concludes by offering a comprehensive simulation study that validates the proposed method.

We introduce a new method for synthesizing novel views of dynamic, unstructured scenes. This approach utilizes a self-supervised neural radiance model that learns to map a scene's appearance to its underlying 3D structure. The system is trained using a combination of RGB-D data and motion capture (MoCap) skeleton data, enabling it to generate novel perspectives that accurately reflect both the geometry and motion of objects. The model is capable of rendering high-quality images at 1024×1024 resolution in under 0.1 seconds. Additionally, it can generate 3D point clouds and meshes, and it is adaptable to various data formats, including those from LiDAR and RGB-D sensors.

We introduce a new method for calculating leading-order random matrix theory predictions for chaotic quantum graphs by utilizing primitive periodic orbits. Specifically, we derive explicit formulas for the spectral form factor and the spectral correlation function applicable to graphs with vertex-transitive or 2-regular structures. Additionally, we present a general formula for the spectral density edge, which is valid for any graph type.

Variable stars are essential for numerous astronomical investigations, including determining distances to galaxies, mapping the universe's expansion, and understanding stellar evolution. Accurately identifying their periods is crucial for these endeavors. This study introduces a novel method for estimating periods using the Lomb-Scargle periodogram, which leverages the periodogram's density estimation properties to pinpoint peaks. We demonstrate that the method's performance is highly sensitive to the smoothing parameter. Consequently, we develop a new approach to estimate this parameter by applying the Minimum Description Length principle to the Lomb-Scargle periodogram's density estimate. Our results indicate that this technique yields superior outcomes compared to existing methods.

Feedback control loops featuring negative imaginary (NI) systems have garnered significant attention due to their inherent stability properties. This paper presents a new approach to the robust stabilization of such NI-based feedback configurations by integrating the concepts of dissipative systems and integral quadratic constraints (IQCs). The proposed methodology is applicable to broader classes of feedback systems, not limited to those involving NI plants. Furthermore, the paper introduces a new class of frequency-weighted NI systems, referred to as frequency-weighted NI systems (FWNI), and establishes the corresponding stability criteria for these structures.

Code-switching (CS) involves mixing two or more languages within a single utterance, a common occurrence in multilingual settings that enhances communication efficiency. While recent advancements in CS detection have primarily focused on bilingual contexts, the scarcity of research on multilingual scenarios hinders progress in this area. To address this, the present study introduces the Multilingual Code-Switching Detection (MCS) corpus, a dataset comprising 1,000 manually annotated multilingual tweets. This corpus covers six language pairs: Arabic-English, Bengali-English, French-English, Hindi-English, Spanish-English, and Turkish-English. We evaluated four state-of-the-art CS detection models using this dataset, achieving F1-scores ranging from 71.4% to 78.2%.

This study examines the three critical unresolved issues in particle physics and cosmology: the nature of dark matter, the origin of neutrino masses, and the cause of baryon asymmetry. We introduce a model that addresses all three simultaneously by extending the Standard Model with a $U(1)_{B-L}$ gauge symmetry and introducing a single right-handed neutrino. This framework yields a dark matter candidate with a mass scale of approximately 10 GeV, which falls within the detection capabilities of current experiments. Furthermore, the model's predictions for lepton flavor violating decays and neutrino oscillation parameters align with existing experimental data.

Predicting user responses to web pages is crucial for enhancing user experience and driving business outcomes. While deep models have recently surpassed traditional approaches in accuracy, they often demand extensive training data and incur high computational costs. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel method that leverages a user's historical clickstream to forecast their reaction to a specific webpage. Our approach utilizes a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to model the sequence of previously visited pages, incorporating temporal dependencies to generate a user embedding. This representation is then combined with the target page's features to predict the desired outcome. We validate our method using a large-scale dataset from a leading Chinese e-commerce platform, demonstrating that our model outperforms both traditional and deep learning baselines.

This study investigates the performance of intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) within cell-free networks, specifically focusing on the impact of IRS placement on channel estimation and data transmission. We model IRS deployment as a two-dimensional Poisson point process (PPP) and derive closed-form expressions for the probability of coverage and the ergodic rate, contingent on the distances between users and the reflecting panels. Our analysis reveals that IRS placement is the primary determinant of performance gains in cell-free architectures. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these gains diminish as the number of IRS elements increases. Additionally, the study shows that the performance benefits of IRS are more pronounced in dense networks compared to sparse ones.

Deep learning has recently been applied to branch prediction, yielding promising results. However, the majority of prior research has focused on utilizing deep learning for prediction within a single processor core. This study introduces a new method that leverages deep learning to forecast branches across an entire multi-core system. The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning model trained on specific thread identifiers and their corresponding thread history files to anticipate outcomes for every core. Experimental results indicate that this method surpasses existing state-of-the-art deep learning-based predictors in both prediction accuracy and performance efficiency.

Visual active monitoring is essential for numerous real-world applications, including surveillance and traffic management. While imitation learning has proven effective in enhancing reinforcement learning, its application to visual active monitoring remains unexplored. This study introduces a new approach that leverages imitation learning to train a policy for visual active monitoring. We demonstrate that this method surpasses standard reinforcement learning by offering greater sample efficiency and robustness to hyperparameters. Furthermore, we propose a reward function grounded in human heuristics to facilitate effective deep imitation learning. Experimental results indicate that our approach yields significant performance gains in both synthetic environments and real-world scenarios.

This study examines the boundary law for the solid-on-solid (SOS) model on a Cayley tree, a system defined by boundary conditions that yield a specific boundary spin configuration. We demonstrate that the boundary law for this model admits non-trivial extremal solutions that are not necessarily constant. Furthermore, we derive a formula for the entropy of these solutions and identify them as entropy maximizers.

This study examines the role of temporal entanglement in the virtual photons responsible for energy transfer between a donor and an acceptor in a quantum system. We demonstrate that this entanglement alters the correlation between the frequencies of these virtual photons, thereby modifying the rate of energy transfer. Specifically, we show that the rate can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude, particularly when the separation distance is large.
We present a concise summary of the strong coupling constants for bottom and charm mesons, derived from the most recent lattice QCD calculations.

The DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande (HK) projects represent two of the most significant initiatives in current neutrino physics, with both experiments aiming to investigate CP violation and the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe, as well as search for neutrino sterile states. This study examines the sensitivity of the DUNE and HK setups to a light sterile neutrino, specifically within the framework of the 3+1 model. Our analysis focuses on the impact of sterile neutrinos on the oscillation probabilities of the HK's 22.5-kiloton water Cherenkov detector and DUNE's 40-kiloton liquid argon time projection chamber, utilizing the respective beam sources and neutrino factories. We evaluate the sensitivity of both experimental configurations to the 3+1 model parameters by analyzing the sensitivity of the oscillation probabilities to the HK's 22.5-kiloton water Cherenkov detector and DUNE's 40-kiloton liquid argon time projection chamber, utilizing the respective beam sources and neutrino factories. In observational research, balancing covariate distribution is crucial for deriving valid causal inferences. While regression-based approaches are widely used to achieve this balance, they often fail to ensure proper distributional alignment. To address this, we introduce a new framework for constructing the optimal propensity score that simultaneously maximizes covariate balance and minimizes overlap, specifically targeting the most robust nonparametric setting. We demonstrate that the proposed optimal propensity score can be derived as the solution to a convex optimization problem. Furthermore, we establish that the optimal propensity score can be estimated consistently. Finally, we validate the theoretical findings through simulation studies and apply the proposed method to a real-world dataset.

This paper introduces a novel, model-free damping control strategy for power systems that leverages deep reinforcement learning (DRL). The approach utilizes rotor speed fluctuations from a generator and the power exchange between two areas to train a deep neural network (DNN) that outputs the necessary damping signal. The training process is designed to optimize a reward function that simultaneously minimizes inter-area oscillations and control effort. The proposed method is evaluated on a 39-bus system experiencing parametric uncertainties, specifically variations in the stiffness of the power system. The results indicate that the DRL-based, model-free controller effectively dampens inter-area oscillations and maintains robust performance despite such stiffness uncertainties.

This study examines the collective radiance of an atomic ensemble containing two excited atoms. We demonstrate that the concurrent decay of these atoms generates a non-linear component in the radiated field, which can be characterized through both mean values and higher-order moments of the field distribution. Additionally, we analyze how the non-classical properties of this collective field evolve over time.

This work investigates the local asymptotic stability of kinks within the gradient flow on the Sobolev space $H^1(\mathbb{R})$ associated with a double-well potential. We demonstrate a sufficient condition ensuring the local asymptotic stability of such kinks under odd perturbations. Furthermore, we illustrate that this stability is not guaranteed for kinks in the case of odd perturbations outside the $H^1$ framework.

This article examines the phenomenon of color transparency within the context of high-energy hadron physics. We present a phenomenological analysis of color transparency effects observed in the nuclear transparency of pions and proton beams, as well as in the nuclear cross-section suppression of $J/\psi$ mesons. Our investigation covers interactions occurring at central rapidities and across transverse momenta ranging from the GeV scale down to the hundreds-of-MeV range.

Consistency training involves learning a model that maintains predictions for an input alongside a closely perturbed version of itself. This methodology has proven effective in enhancing various tasks, including image classification, denoising, and segmentation. However, existing techniques typically rely on pixel-space perturbations, which can be computationally expensive and hinder the application of this approach to high-resolution imagery. This paper introduces a novel, resolution-independent consistency training framework that leverages data from the latent space. By utilizing this new approach, we achieve improved results on image classification and segmentation tasks, particularly in scenarios with limited data. The proposed technique is compatible with both shallow and deep neural architectures. Empirical results indicate that our method surpasses state-of-the-art performance in classification and segmentation when trained on smaller datasets.

This study introduces a novel framework for polyp localization in gastrointestinal endoscopy videos, leveraging a deep learning approach that integrates a recurrent neural network (RNN) with a convolutional neural network (CNN). The architecture utilizes the CNN to extract features from individual frames, while the RNN component processes a sequence of these frames to mitigate variations between them and reduce artifacts caused by frame dropping. This mechanism enhances localization precision, particularly in videos with low frame rates. The proposed method was evaluated on the Kvasir-SEG dataset, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This paper introduces a novel approach to unequal probability sampling that is specifically designed for a fixed population divided into $K$ strata. The method, which utilizes a sliding window technique, ensures that the inclusion probability for each element is known beforehand. The proposed algorithm is straightforward to implement and offers significant computational efficiency. Theoretical proofs confirm that the inclusion probabilities are calculable in advance and that the sampling design is self-normalizing. Additionally, the study evaluates the method's finite population bias and variance through a simulation analysis. The results demonstrate that the design achieves unbiasedness and variance that aligns well with theoretical expectations.

This study reports a measurement of the half-life for the doubly magic nucleus $^{57}$Zn, yielding a value of $14.6(3)\text{ s}$. The research utilized the FRIB facility to generate $^{57}$Zn via the $^{58}$Fe($p,2p$) reaction, which was subsequently implanted into the EXACT detector array. The analysis involved identifying the decay of $^{57}$Zn through its characteristic $\gamma$-ray emissions and correlating these events with implantation signals.
This work generalizes the findings of [Mim18] to establish a bijective relationship between special 0-cycles and special div格 classes on abelian schemes defined over rings of integers.

Pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) are known to emit across the electromagnetic spectrum, with their optical and X-ray emissions primarily attributed to synchrotron radiation from relativistic electrons and positrons. However, the origins of their radio emissions remain uncertain, with two primary hypotheses: either the synchrotron process extends into the radio band, or radio emission arises from a distinct mechanism, such as coherent processes. This study investigates the radio emission of the Crab nebula by analyzing the temporal evolution of its radio flux density at 1.4 GHz. We employed a new method to derive the nebula's proper motion from archival VLBA data, enabling us to calculate proper motion maps for the radio structure. By comparing these maps with optical proper motion data from the Hubble Space Telescope, we determined that the motions of the Crab nebula's radio and optical regions are consistent with each other. Consequently, we conclude that the radio emission originates from synchrotron radiation, implying that the emitting electrons and positrons in the radio range share the same origin and acceleration mechanism as those producing optical synchrotron emission.

This study examines the existence of an attractor within a family of weak solutions for a reaction-diffusion equation characterized by a variable absorption term. The proof relies on a novel approach that integrates recent findings regarding compact global attractors for equations with a specific type of superlinear absorption.

We present a novel, automated method for identifying Ultra-compact dwarfs (UCDs) and Globular Clusters (GCs) using deep learning. This approach leverages the recently developed DeepClusterFinder (DCF) framework, which utilizes a ResNet-50 architecture to classify objects based on their images. By applying DCF to the Hubble Space Telescope's (HST) Hubble Space Telescope (HST) archive, we have identified 1,000 new UCDs and GCs. This catalog is made available to the public. Additionally, we have developed a new classification scheme that categorizes UCDs and GCs into three distinct groups: those with a stellar population dominated by old stars, those dominated by young stars, and those with a mixed stellar population. This scheme is based on the color-magnitude diagram (CMD) of each object, which is constructed using the photometric data from the HST. Recommender Systems (RS) are essential for assisting users in discovering relevant items within vast repositories. However, developing effective RS remains challenging due to data sparsity, cold-start issues, and the need for interpretability. To address these hurdles, researchers have created various explainable RS (XRS) methods that generate recommendations alongside rationales. Despite this progress, XRS is still in its infancy, and a comprehensive review of existing approaches is lacking. This paper presents a survey of XRS, offering a systematic overview of current techniques. We begin by defining XRS and detailing the metrics used to evaluate them. Next, we categorize existing XRS methods into four distinct types based on the nature of the explanations they provide. We then analyze the primary challenges facing XRS and suggest potential future research directions. Finally, we conclude with a summary of the paper's contributions.

This study examines the asymptotic behavior of the sample mean and sample variance under heavy-tailed conditions, specifically focusing on distributions with infinite Fisher information. We introduce truncated estimators for both parameters and demonstrate that their asymptotic distribution approaches normality, even when the underlying distribution is heavy-tailed, provided the truncation threshold increases sufficiently rapidly. We further analyze the consistency of truncated estimators derived from truncated U-statistics and establish that they achieve asymptotic normality. Additionally, the paper derives the finite sample distribution of the truncated test statistic and illustrates its application in hypothesis testing for heavy-tailed data.

Controlling devices through the brain is a longstanding aspiration, and Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCI) have realized this by translating electroencephalogram (EEG) signals into commands. While current BCI systems can manage simple motions like cursors, robotic arms, and prosthetics, they fall short of replicating the natural, fluid movements humans perform. This study introduces a new BCI framework that leverages a deep learning model to transform EEG data into continuous, smooth trajectories. The system employs a deep neural network to extract features from raw EEG inputs and a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to generate smooth control signals. These refined signals are then processed by a PID controller to ensure movement fluidity. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully manages continuous motion with high precision and low error rates.

We determine the conformal two-point function for scalar operators in non-unitary conformal field theories (CTFTs) by utilizing conformal symmetry alongside a negative spectral gap. This process yields a new class of conformal cross-ratio functions that are positive definite for unitary theories but become sign-indefinite in the context of non-unitary ones. These functions serve as the Fourier coefficients of conformal block families and are defined as solutions to a specific hypergeometric differential equation.

Rejection of the transplanted organ is a significant challenge when performing kidney transplants on recipients whose immune systems are incompatible with their donors. Although pre-transplant desensitization therapies can lower rejection risks, these treatments often cause severe side effects. Consequently, there is a critical need for personalized, non-invasive interventions that effectively prevent graft rejection while minimizing adverse reactions. This study introduces a new approach utilizing a non-linear optimal control framework to dynamically adjust the levels of two key immunosuppressive drugs. The objective is to suppress T-cell proliferation while strictly adhering to safety limits on drug concentrations. The proposed methodology is validated through numerical simulations based on a mathematical model of the human immune system.

Experience management applications are increasingly being adopted to gather and analyze user feedback. However, their widespread adoption is hindered by the high costs associated with data labeling and the need for specialized expertise. To address this, we introduce a multi-task modeling framework that leverages data from related domains to enhance the quality of user experience insights. Our approach utilizes a multi-task learning architecture to jointly model the target domain and a related domain, thereby improving performance through the shared learning of related tasks. We further implement a dynamic task selection mechanism to identify and incorporate only the most pertinent information from the related domain, ensuring that irrelevant or noisy data does not degrade model outcomes. Experimental results demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art solutions in both accuracy and efficiency.

Open data represents a pivotal component of the broader open science framework. This presentation will explore the current landscape of open data initiatives within high-energy physics and examine prospective paths forward.

We introduce a novel method for constructing generic Richelot isogenies by decomposing them into four distinct Jacobian isogenies. This approach facilitates both a more efficient traversal of Richelot graphs and the development of new Siegel modular varieties.

We report the inaugural detection of a magnetic field in a hot subdwarf (sdB) star, HD 100630, utilizing the Zeeman broadening technique. This measurement yields a magnetic fraction ($f_B$) of approximately $10^{-4}$, which is roughly 100 times lower than the lower limit established for hot sdBs by previous studies. This result is consistent with the magnetic fraction observed in hot pre-white dwarfs (pBDA) and suggests that magnetic fields in hot compact stars may be more prevalent than previously thought. The detection of a magnetic field in HD 100630 is likely attributable to the presence of a convective core, which facilitates the generation of magnetic fields through dynamo action.

Positive semi-definite (PSD) matrices are fundamental to various statistical and machine learning applications, notably covariance estimation. This paper addresses covariance estimation for a sequence of distributions, where each distribution is characterized by a distinct PSD matrix. We introduce a new framework for learning these matrices that integrates both spectral and entry-wise distance metrics. Our approach involves a novel hypothesis class of matrices that are $\epsilon$-close spectrally to a specific target PSD matrix and belong within an $L_1$ ball of radius $r$ relative to the Frobenius matrix. We demonstrate that this class is PAC learnable, with a sample complexity of $\tilde{O}(r^2/\epsilon + \log(1/\delta))$. Furthermore, we present a corresponding algorithm that matches this complexity. Our methodology relies on a new spectral sparsification technique for the exponential family of distributions, which is of independent interest.

Wikipedia stands as the world's largest online encyclopedia, boasting over 55 million articles that are authored and edited by a vast community of contributors. Structurally, Wikipedia's content resides within a wiki tree, where each node represents an article composed of multiple sections, each containing one or more paragraphs. This hierarchical organization is defined by the MediaWiki software, which stores the page content in a format known as wikitext. While wikitext is designed for efficient storage and retrieval, it is not optimized for immediate content analysis. In contrast, HTML serves as the standard markup for web pages and is more conducive to analyzing Wikipedia's textual material. This study presents a method for converting wikitext into HTML by leveraging the MediaWiki parser, which generates HTML from wikitext using an internal template system. We evaluate this approach by comparing it to an alternative method that relies on the MediaWiki internal parser. Our findings indicate that the proposed method offers superior performance in terms of both speed and accuracy.

The primary cosmological probes for investigating the universe's properties, including spatial curvature, are the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO). While the CMB is highly sensitive to curvature, it is inherently degenerate with the angular diameter distance to the last scattering surface. In contrast, BAO measurements are largely independent of this distance but are less sensitive to curvature. By combining these two probes, researchers can break the associated degeneracies. This study examines the spatial curvature constraints derived from the Planck 2018 CMB data when paired with BAO data from the 6dF, SDSS-IV, and 2dF surveys. We also investigate the impact of varying neutrino mass priors on curvature constraints. Our results indicate that the 6dF+Planck combination yields a curvature constraint of $\Omega_{k}=0.000\pm0.002$, which aligns with the Planck 2018 findings. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the 6dF+Planck dataset provides the tightest curvature limits to date when no prior information on neutrino mass is assumed.

This study examines the dynamics of a colloidal particle within a nematic liquid crystal subjected to a localized external force. The particle's trajectory is governed by energy landscapes resulting from the nematic's anisotropy, which creates regions of both potential wells and barriers. We demonstrate that the particle can become trapped in metastable states, leading to bistability, and we derive an analytical expression for the probability of escaping these states. Furthermore, we show that a stochastic force can induce the particle to move against the gradient of the nematic field, effectively overcoming the deterministic force that pulls it toward the bulk liquid.

This study examines how the shape of an asteroid influences the YORP effect during flybys of planets other than Earth. We find that during distant planetary encounters, the variation in surface slope ($\Delta i$) is significantly larger for elongated objects compared to spherical ones. For instance, an asteroid with an elongation of 1.5 experiences a $\Delta i$ that is 2.5 times greater than that of a sphere. This heightened $\Delta i$ leads to substantial changes in the asteroid's spin rate, potentially resulting in spin-reversal or even breakup. Consequently, these findings suggest that the YORP effect is more potent during distant planetary encounters than previously recognized.

Structural reconfigurations are fundamental to the function of biomolecular systems, ranging from the conformational transitions of proteins to the dynamic movements of cells. These rearrangements are typically characterized by a small set of collective variables that define the reaction coordinate. This study introduces a methodology to identify such collective variables by utilizing the optimal transport framework. Our approach is demonstrated on a simplified model of a two-state protein folding process, where the reaction coordinate is defined by the count of native contacts. We evaluate the performance of our technique by applying it to both the full molecular dynamics trajectory and various coarse-grained trajectories.

We introduce the inaugural polarimetric observations of the blazar 3C 273 at 1.3 mm, conducted using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA). The data reveal a linear polarization fraction of 10.5% ± 1.5% and a magnetic field orientation of 110° ± 10° relative to the line of sight. These findings align with previous ALMA results from the nearby blazar 3C 454.3, which exhibited a similar polarization fraction of 10% ± 5%. The polarization angle indicates a magnetic field structure that is either ordered or predominantly toroidal. Furthermore, these results are consistent with a synchrotron emission mechanism, suggesting that the magnetic field is likely ordered or toroidal in nature.

We demonstrate that the ice thickness evolves toward a steady state, $g_{\rm st}(h)$, which is a function of the wind stress $\tau$ and the critical thickness $h_{\rm c}$. Let $K$ be a field and $n_1, \ldots, n_r$ be a collection of integers. We define the generalized Weierstrass semigroup $\mathcal{H}(n_1, \ldots, n_r)$ as the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}_0^r$ comprising the multi-integer valuations associated with rational functions on the algebraic curve resulting from the product of $r$ copies of the algebraic closure $\overline{K}$. In this work, we establish several novel results regarding this semigroup, specifically addressing its cardinality, the count of its minimal generators, and the structure of its minimal generating set.

Recent technological breakthroughs have significantly enhanced the quality and realism of speech synthesis, yet generating singing voice remains a formidable challenge. This study introduces a new singing voice synthesis framework that leverages deep learning to produce high-fidelity vocals. The architecture comprises two primary modules: a feature extraction component utilizing a modified WaveNet model, and a synthesis module built upon a conditional WaveNet structure. This system was evaluated against existing methods using objective metrics, including Mel Cepstral Distortion (MCD) and Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI), as well as subjective listening tests. The results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms current state-of-the-art singing synthesis approaches.

The availability of extensive, fully annotated recordings is crucial for advancing research in birdsong detection and classification. This paper introduces Birdnet-100, a dataset comprising 100 bird species from Birdnet, each represented by 100-second clips with precise start and end annotations. These recordings were generated by processing 100-hour segments of the Xeno-Canto database using a trained model designed to identify birdsong. Additionally, we provide a pre-trained model capable of detecting bird song in new audio data. Our experimental results demonstrate that this model surpasses existing approaches in both birdsong detection and classification tasks.

Event cameras are increasingly utilized in computer vision, yet their calibration remains a challenging task. This paper introduces a new method for calibrating event cameras by leveraging the complementary nature of pixel and event data. Specifically, we propose a novel calibration approach that utilizes a neural network to reconstruct images from event streams. This method eliminates the need for a separate pixel camera, thereby reducing hardware costs. Additionally, we present a new calibration algorithm that integrates pixel image data with event streams, enabling the determination of both extrinsic and intrinsic parameters. This framework can also recover motion information from the camera. To evaluate our approach, we developed a new benchmark dataset featuring a pixel camera paired with an event camera. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in both accuracy and robustness.

Graph learning has emerged as a vital field within machine learning, driven by the growing prevalence of graph-structured data in real-world scenarios. Unlike traditional tabular formats, these data types inherently possess complex, intricate relationships. This paper introduces a novel, unsupervised graph learning framework designed to derive a unified embedding space for both nodes and edges. By employing a dual-level graph neural network, the model simultaneously captures node and edge features. Furthermore, it integrates a graph convolutional autoencoder to learn node representations, utilizing a contrastive loss function to optimize the embedding space. To refine edge representations, the method incorporates a contrastive loss function grounded in graph structural information. Experimental results on three public datasets demonstrate that this approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

This work examines exceptional objects located on the left-hand side within the Auslander-Reiten quiver of an algebraically reduced weak del Pezzo surface. We demonstrate that such objects can be constructed through kernels of specific morphisms between line bundles. Furthermore, we establish a connection between these objects and the concept of relative exceptional collections. Finally, we provide a classification of all exceptional objects with dimension 1, which are found to be of the form $E_1 \oplus \dots \oplus E_n$.
